verses.verse:
तिव्राधातेन प्राणस्य क्रमसः पूर्व वद्यदा।
सप्तानाम् नादनम् कुर्यात् तदा नादा श्चतुर्दश।८७।
verses.text: When, with a strong stroke of breath, one sounds the seven in order as before, then there are fourteen sounds.

commentary.text: If in this way one keeps lifting the fingers as before while increasing the strength of the breath, the seven notes of the second octave will be produced. So it is proved that by increasing the force of the breath the same seven sounds have gone into another octave — just as any number, on gaining a zero, changes from units to tens. But by blowing harder still, only two or three notes of the third octave can come out. In this way, in a flute with six holes, usually a total of 15 śuddha (natural) notes are produced, in this order: Sa Re Ga Ma Pa Dha Ni | Ṡa Ṙe Ġa Ṁa Ṗa Ḋha Ṅi | Ṡa. For the remaining komal notes, the method of opening less than half a hole has to be adopted. In a flute with eight holes there are holes for komal Ga and komal Dha as well.
